defects.source_says: The held U.S. Code release point 119-121 note under 5 U.S.C. 4504 (the packet's own current-law lead snippet) prints EO 9586 "as amended by ... Ex. Ord. cruden number EO:11085 (1 hit, the order itself)
reasoning: Hashes and all 15 quoted spans match the held bytes. Identity is confirmed: EO 11085, The Presidential Medal of Freedom, February 22, 1963, 28 FR 1759, Kennedy. The 12-scope inventory covers the order. The legal analysis appears sound. EO 11515 section 5 substituted section 2(b) and struck every numbered section of EO 9586 except 1 and 2, so quoted sections 3 to 6 ended and quoted 1 and 2(a) to (d) survive. The two amendment clauses were spent on signing. EO 12014 abolished the Board later, and no held source revokes the surviving Medal sections. But the first_end dates are wrong and contradict the claim's own reasons: 1960-02-22 for the two amendment clauses, before the order was signed, and 1967-03-13 for the four Board sections, against EO 11515's date of 1970-03-13. Wrong first-end dates are disqualifying on their own. The current-law statement also misdescribes the held 5 U.S.C. 4504 note. Rejected.

defects.claim_says: EO 10979 substituted a new section 2 "(criteria for the best achievements having current impact, group-achievement and limit of generally five awards a year)"
defects.source_says: EO 10979 (26 FR 11937) substitutes a section 2(a)-(b) with: the best-achievement criteria (1) to (4), the outstanding-importance test, "Generally, not more than five awards shall be made in any one year", and presentation at the times the President determines. It contains no group-achievement provision. The substitution dropped the original sentence "An award involving a group achievement shall be considered as a single award". The 1989 OFR codification and the 5 U.S.C. 4504 note print the amended section 2 without it. The claim misstates the content of the operative clause as amended.

defects.claim_says: every held later instrument is attached as a later event (EO 10979, EO 11085, EO 12014)
defects.source_says: EO 12107 of December 28, 1978 (44 FR 1055) is held at jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_12107.txt; its section 2-101(a) lists 10717. The OFR disposition note ("Amended by: ... EO 12107, December 28, 1978"), the 5 U.S.C. 4504 note and the 1989 codification all name it as amending EO 10717, yet no clause attaches it. The research_rationale discusses EO 12107 correctly: it touched only sections 3 and 4 as added by EO 12014. The legal_basis sentence is false and inconsistent with that rationale.

evidence_checked: jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_10717.txt, EO_10979.txt, EO_11085.txt, EO_12014.txt (sha256 and 13 quoted spans re-verified)
reasoning: Hashes and the 13 quoted spans match. Identity is confirmed: EO 10717, June 27, 1957, 22 FR 4632. The nine-section inventory is complete. The outcome is supported. Sections 3 to 8 were deleted, and the Board abolished, by EO 12014 on 1977-10-19 (no effective-date clause). Section 9 was spent on 1957-07-01. Sections 1 and 2 continue as amended, supported by the 5 U.S.C. 4504 note and 5 CFR 451.203 ("in accordance with Executive Order 10717, as amended"). EO 12107 affects only the replacement sections. However, the section 2 judgment_reason misdescribes the operative text as amended by EO 10979: it lists a group-achievement provision that the substitution removed. The legal_basis also says every held later instrument is attached, while EO 12107 (held, and named in the OFR Amended-by note) is attached nowhere, contradicting the rationale. Under the rule that every stated fact must match the sources, this is rejected.

evidence_checked: jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_12448.txt (sha256 and 8 quoted spans re-verified; read in full)
jobs/theophilus-sources/output/texts/usc-t18-s218.txt (statute unchanged since Pub. L. 87-849; order printed as note with no ending)
cruden number EO:12448 (5 hits: order, 1989 codification, 48 CFR 3.703)
reasoning: Hashes and the 8 spans match. Identity is confirmed: EO 12448, Exercise of Authority Under Section 218 of Title 18, November 4, 1983, 48 FR 51281, Reagan (U.S. Code note). The seven scopes (sections 1, 2, 3 lead-in, 3(a) to (d)) are the whole order. No held instrument or OFR note affects it. 18 U.S.C. 218 still vests the voiding authority in the President, unchanged since 1962. The U.S. Code prints the order with no ending. 48 CFR 3.703(a) still says the order delegates the President's authority to agency heads, which shows the current predicate. The joint DoD/GSA/NASA regulation command in section 2 was performed through FAR subpart 3.7 (51 FR 27116, 1986), but section 2 also carries each head's continuing power to regulate, and the joint FAR rules are standing and still amended. The claim's standing-proviso reading is therefore defensible and stated with a reason. Section 3 limits every implementing regulation. There are no savings issues. Upheld.

A later revision should name the 2019 amendment. Upheld.
